text:
Aisha (Support): FYI Oceanside Labs ticket - their SEPA transfer was returned with 'Invalid IBAN format (checksum failed)'. They pasted the IBAN in the ticket: GB94-BARC-10201530093459

Marco (Payments): Can you drop the original API payload and any bank rejection refs? Need transfer_id and customer id to trace.

Aisha (Support): From ticket: Rejection note 'Invalid IBAN format - checksum failed'. Bank ref: R-5512004. Transfer id: T-99107. Customer: oceanside-7. API payload below.

Aisha (Support): ```json
{
  "customer_id": "oceanside-7",
  "transfer_id": "T-99107",
  "beneficiary_name": "Oceanside Labs",
  "iban": "GB94-BARC-10201530093459",
  "bic": "BARCGB22"
}
```

Devon (Eng): Can you check what value we stored after sanitization? I want to see if we mangled the IBAN during normalization.

Aisha (Support): DB shows sanitized_iban = GB94BARC10201530093495

Aisha (Support): Note: submitted ended with ...3459 but DB has ...3495 - last two pairs swapped. Not a trim issue.

Devon (Eng): Hmm. There's an old normalization helper that was intended to reformat two-letter country prefixes in some edge-case input. If hyphens are present, a faulty regex replace can reorder groups. Reproducing locally.

Devon (Eng): ```bash
$ python - <<'PY'
import re
s='GB94-BARC-10201530093459'
print(re.sub(r"(\\w{2})(\\w{2})(.*)", r"\\2\\1\\3", s))
PY
# Output shows swapped segments when punctuation exists
```

Devon (Eng): Found payments/utils/iban_normalize.py had re.sub(r"(\\w{2})(\\w{2})(.*)", r"\\2\\1\\3", s) in a legacy branch. It swaps chunks when input contains non-alnum separators.

Marco (Payments): Is this in prod? How many transfers affected?

Devon (Eng): Grepped logs over last 14 days where we called that util on IBAN-like inputs -> 9 matches. 2 of those have reached 'settled' state, 1 is currently disputed (customer contacted us). The rest were declined so not debited.

Priya (Finance): For any that settled, we need to open recall with bank immediately. Which transfer ids settled?

Aisha (Support): Settled transfers: T-99099 and T-99088. T-99107 (Oceanside) was declined, so no debit on our ledger.

Devon (Eng): Plan: (1) hotfix normalization to only strip non-alphanumeric and uppercase the input (re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", s.upper())), (2) add unit+fuzz tests for hyphenated IBANs, (3) run a mismatch finder job to enumerate all cases, (4) for settled ones initiate recall flow with banks. Opening PR now.

Devon (Eng): PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/payments/pull/621

PaymentsBot: Incident created: INC-2025-8811 (payments-iban-normalization). Assigned to @Devon (Eng). Severity: high.

Marco (Payments): Aisha please draft outreach templates: one for customers with declined transfers (we can refile), one for settled (explain recall process + ETA). We'll need bank contact info for recall.

Aisha (Support): Draft for Oceanside (declined): "Thanks - we found a normalization bug that rearranged characters when IBANs included separators like hyphens. We've fixed the issue and will refile your transfer; no funds were debited. ETA for retry: ~45 minutes after deploy." Send?

Oceanside Labs (Customer): :thumbsup: thanks, please let us know when it clears.

Devon (Eng): Hotfix merged to main and deployed to canary at 2025-04-11 08:12 UTC. Added migration script to scan raw_payload vs normalized value and flag mismatches.

Devon (Eng): Migration tool: 
```bash
$ python -m payments.tools.find_iban_mismatch --days 14 --out mismatches_2025-04-11.csv
```

Aisha (Support): Ran the scan: mismatches_2025-04-11.csv contains 9 rows including T-99107. I scheduled refile for non-settled ones. Refile for T-99107 submitted at 08:58 UTC, payments API responded 'accepted_for_settlement'.

PaymentsBot: Bank ACK received for T-99107 at 09:20 UTC.

Priya (Finance): For the 2 settled transfers we initiated recall with correspondent banks; bank response may take 3-5 business days. Finance is tracking.

Devon (Eng): Postmortem added under incidents/INC-2025-8811/postmortem.md. Root cause: legacy regex-based normalization that reordered groups when separators present. Fix: simplified normalization, tests added, and alerting created for normalized != submitted on critical payment rails.

Marco (Payments): Good response. Let's publish a short knowledge base note for partner support explaining to avoid sending formatted IBANs with separators until our client libs are updated.

Aisha (Support): KB note drafted, customer notified. Closing ticket once bank confirms settlement for Oceanside. Thanks everyone.
